item.content:encoded:
Having read your explanation, I understand it. So a counter below, and I say this because I believe this tale could have been better if there was actually more to it.

Prologues can stand on their own. A prologue may be able to set up the rest of a series, but it can still be enjoyable to read without context. Ideally, that's what it should be. ALERT! LOCKDOWN INITIATED! managed to be very enjoyable with setting up its characters and setting, Conspiracy's Prologue helps to set the tension and action of the series, and though wowwee go kill ursefl is incredibly short, it sets up context for the series, as well as make the situation entertaining and resolve its build and climax by the end. Hell, I'm even going to bring up your own A World's Legacy, because I enjoyed the shit out of that, and the worldbuilding and interweaving of various skips to form the fantasy land was a great read.

This isn't a bad tale, and I'm not saying it is. Up until this bit:

"Sorry love, can't have you interfering just yet. Too dangerous for you."

I was incredibly into the tale, and the use of 033, and wondering where this was going to go. By the time I hit that, I realized your threads were going to resolve suddenly despite the rest of the tale seeming like I was going to get more, instead of an abrupt and sudden change. And I've read Colourless Green, and I enjoyed that, but this tale didn't help me think of that tale, and I never connected the two. In the end, they seem like unrelated works who's only connection is antimemetics. And antimemetics is becoming common enough now where I know what I like in it, and while I don't expect action sequences or deep philosophy, I don't like having the chain yanked to an unsatisfying conclusion.

I hope this didn't come off as mean-spirited. I'm trying to be honest about my feelings in regards to this tale, because 3/θ' of it is very enjoyable, and it's that final bit that just kills it for me. And knowing the information here kills it even more for me, especially because that's intentional.

item.content:encoded:
Aaaaand now to hopefully give you a satisfactory explanation for why this is so short.

I had been talking things over with qntm during the conceptualization and early drafting of this tale. At the time, he had also been working on CASE COLOURLESS GREEN. After some deliberation, this tale was set up as a prologue to that tale, with this one hinting at and taking place before CCG. I couldn't say too much in this tale without ruining a lot of the punch for that one. As it is, now that that tale is available to the general public…

+ Moar Spoilers
– hide block

You may want to read this post and my earlier spoilers for a bit more context.

"█████" is SCP-3125. That hole full of whitespace used to refer to what SCP-3125 was from the angle that the Counterconceptual division was looking at it. It would have wiped them out too, had Liz (an antimemetic weapon like Clay and Grey) not already gone AWOL and sided with the Foundation. As it was, she was able to wipe the memory of it just before it had a chance to get all of the division, giving them a chance to pick themselves up and rebuild.

So for those of you who felt that this was going somewhere and then cut off, you're absolutely right, and it was intentional.

item.title: Tale!
item.content:encoded:
Another piece of antimemetics/counterconceptual mischief. Thanks to Athena_Gray, thekillerax, and MacLeod for looking this over. Big thanks to qntm for looking this over and helping me plan it out.

Anomalies:

  • "█████": a highly virulent anomaly with a mix of infohazard and antimeme properties. Highly dangerous to humans in general, but especially people on mnestics.
  • SCP-i: i as in the square root of negative one, the "imaginary number." Was originally the documentation for █████ before becoming highly hazardous itself because of the subject matter.
  • Liz Day: A humanoid antimeme. She works by de-aging people so that, from their perspective, certain memories never even formed.
  • SCP-θ': An added layer of anomalous security to keep information about █████ and SCP-i hidden.
SPOILERS
– hide block

Liz Day in an antimeme in human form in the same vein as Clay and Grey. All three of them are antimemetic "warheads" sent to attack the Foundation. The difference is that, unlike Clay and Grey, Liz has defected to the Foundation. The casualties in the NIGHT MIRROR incident were caused by two separate anomalies; one was █████, which caused the uncountable number of casualties, while the second was Liz, trying to wipe █████ from the CCD before it got to all of them.
